source.title: dilemmas and outcomes.pdf
source.changes: De-identified and reworded; question in yes/no form.

suggested_action: ambush and kill the ruler of your country
kept: You remain an army officer and a member of the group seeking change without civil war.
The ruler has ordered thousands of killings on ethnic or political grounds over decades.
You consider killing unavoidable to remove the ruler, family and followers from power; six others join the ambush.
You directly participate in killing one ruler; the alternative is continued killings by the regime.
Change is a chance, not a guaranteed peaceful transition; personal benefit is not specified beyond your membership in the country.
The suggested action is to kill the ruler, not his family or followers.
rewrite: You are an army officer in a country whose ruler has governed as a dictator for decades. He has had thousands of people killed for their ethnicity or political views. You belong to a group seeking a new beginning for the country without civil war. You believe killing the ruler is unavoidable if he, his family and his followers are to lose power. You and six fellow conspirators are asked to ambush and kill him. If you kill the ruler, the people of your country will have a chance of a new beginning. If you do not, his regime will go on killing. Do you kill the ruler?
notes: The ruler’s nationality and period are removed. Political and ethnic persecution, the family power structure and the number of conspirators remain; these may still identify the incident.
